key_terms.meaning: A 7-tuple (Q, Σ, Γ, δ, q0, Z0, F) with finite control and one stack.
Unbounded last-in-first-out memory that stores symbols from the stack alphabet Γ.
δ(q, a, Z) gives possible (p, γ): in state q, on input a and top Z, go to p and replace Z by γ.
(q, w, γ): current state q, unread input w, and stack contents γ read top to bottom.
One step of a PDA changes one ID to another by applying δ and consuming at most one input symbol.
Initial stack symbol that marks the bottom of the stack.
A PDA accepts w if (q0, w, Z0) leads to some (q, ε, γ) with q ∈ F.
A PDA accepts w if (q0, w, Z0) leads to (q, ε, ε) for some state q.
From any final-state PDA one can build an empty-stack PDA for the same language, and conversely.
At most one move for each (state, input symbol or ε, stack top).
δ may return several moves, and ε-moves are allowed, so the machine can choose.
A language accepted by some DPDA; a strict subset of the context-free languages.
A derivation that always expands the leftmost variable of the sentential form.
A PDA simulates leftmost derivations by keeping the unexpanded suffix on its stack.
A grammar variable meaning the PDA can move from state p to q while removing stack symbol A.
A parser that starts at the start symbol and predicts a leftmost derivation of the input.
A parser that starts with the input and reduces handles until it reaches the start symbol.
A substring that matches the right side of a production and can be reduced in a bottom-up parse.
A bottom-up method that shifts input symbols onto a stack and reduces handles.
LL predicts a leftmost derivation top-down; LR builds a rightmost derivation in reverse bottom-up.

takeaways: A PDA is a finite automaton plus one stack, so it can match nested pairs but cannot count three independent levels.
An instantaneous description (q, w, γ) records the state, unread input, and full stack; a run is a chain of IDs linked by ⊢.
Acceptance by final state and acceptance by empty stack are interchangeable, so either may be used in definitions.
A DPDA has no choice in any configuration; an NPDA may choose among several moves or take ε-moves.
NPDAs accept exactly the context-free languages, while DPDAs accept the smaller family of deterministic context-free languages.
The CFG-to-PDA construction stores the unexpanded suffix of a leftmost derivation on the stack.
The PDA-to-CFG construction uses variables [p, A, q] that mean the machine can go from p to q while popping A.
Top-down parsing predicts a leftmost derivation from the start symbol; bottom-up parsing shifts input and reduces handles from the leaves upward.
Parsing tables turn PDA ideas into practical linear-time parsers for restricted grammar classes.
bank_note: Long answers usually require the formal PDA tuple with an ID-based run, a construction from a grammar or language, and the two-way CFG–PDA equivalence proof.

glossary.def: A finite automaton with one unbounded last-in-first-out stack.
A last-in-first-out store whose top symbol controls the next PDA move.
The finite set of symbols that may appear on the input tape.
The finite set of symbols that may be pushed on the stack.
The rule that maps state, input symbol or ε, and stack top to possible next moves.
A triple (q, w, γ) giving state, unread input, and stack contents.
The one-step relation ⊢ between instantaneous descriptions.
A special stack symbol placed at the bottom to detect an empty stack.
A state in F; reaching it with empty input is one way to accept.
Acceptance when the PDA reaches empty stack after reading all input.
A PDA with at most one legal move in every configuration.
A PDA that may have several legal moves, including ε-moves.
A language accepted by some deterministic PDA.
A grammar whose productions have one variable on the left.
A derivation that always expands the leftmost variable first.
A substring matching a production right side that a bottom-up parser may reduce.
Parsing that builds the tree from the start symbol down to the input.
Parsing that builds the tree from the input leaves up to the start symbol.
A bottom-up parsing method that shifts input and reduces handles on a stack.
A top-down table-driven parser that reads input left to right and predicts leftmost derivations.
A bottom-up table-driven parser that reads input left to right and builds a rightmost derivation in reverse.
A prefix of a right sentential form that can appear on a shift-reduce parser stack.
A PDA move that consumes no input symbol.
Another name for an instantaneous description of a machine.
